primary_source.title: The Wall Street Explosion Investigation
primary_source.publication: Bureau of Investigation Case Files, National Archives

review_method: Verified against official records of the Bureau of Investigation (precursor to the FBI) and the National Archives (RG 65). On September 16, 1920, at exactly 12:01 PM, a horse-drawn wagon packed with 100 lbs of dynamite and 500 lbs of cast-iron sash weights exploded outside J.P. Morgan & Co. headquarters at 23 Wall Street. Over $30 million in bearer bonds vanished in the blast smoke. Director William J. Flynn led the federal investigation tracing blast-damaged horseshoes and warning leaflets from 'American Anarchist Fighters'. The driver was never identified, leaving it the oldest unsolved terror attack on Wall Street.

claims.paraphrase: Over thirty million dollars in bearer bonds vanished in the blast smoke.
claims.support_summary: FBI historical archives and treasury audit records show over $30 million in bearer bonds, securities, and certificates were destroyed or disappeared in the blast aftermath.

claims.paraphrase: On September 16, 1920, at exactly twelve-o-one PM, a horse-drawn cart stopped outside J.P. Morgan.
claims.support_summary: Official Bureau records document the wagon stopped at 12:01 PM outside 23 Wall Street.

claims.paraphrase: One hundred pounds of dynamite and five hundred pounds of iron weights detonated.
claims.support_summary: Forensic reconstruction by the Bureau of Investigation confirmed approximately 100 lbs of dynamite and 500 lbs of cast-iron window sash weights.

claims.paraphrase: Bureau of Investigation Director William J. Flynn launched the largest federal manhunt in American history.
claims.support_summary: Director Flynn personally directed the nationwide investigation, interviewing thousands of people across the country.

claims.paraphrase: Agents traced the horses shoes and found warning flyers from radical bombers in a nearby mailbox.
claims.support_summary: Investigators tracked the blacksmith who shod the horse and found warning flyers from the 'American Anarchist Fighters' in a mailbox at Wall and Broad Streets.

claims.paraphrase: The driver was never identified, leaving this the oldest unsolved terror attack on Wall Street.
claims.support_summary: Despite years of investigation, the driver of the wagon was never identified or captured.
